facts.text: El Cajon’s name comes from Rancho El Cajón, named for the box‑shaped valley that surrounds the city, earning it the nickname “the Box”.
The El Cajon Valley was originally inhabited by the Kumeyaay people before settlers arrived in the late 1800s.
The old Knox House, once a two‑story hotel, now serves as the El Cajon Historical Society’s museum and community hub.
The East County Performing Arts Center, a renowned concert venue, hosts musicians and Broadway productions right in downtown El Cajon.
Since the 1990s, El Cajon has welcomed immigrants from Iraq and the former Yugoslavia, adding to its cultural mosaic.
The former El Cajon Speedway, once the fastest 3/8‑mile paved oval in the West, now operates as a historic museum with its original entrance sign.
